key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning delivered the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network offered strong shared-learning performance across related welding outputs.
engineering_relevance: For welding process optimization, the study shows that model choice depends on the goal: maximum task-specific accuracy favors stacking, while multitask learning is attractive when related targets and data efficiency matter.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding performance metrics: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness from a shared dataset.
Evaluated models using RMSE and R² to assess predictive error and explained variance.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² across all three targets, with the strongest results for UTS and weld hardness; MTNN still showed solid generalization, especially for weld hardness and HAZ hardness.
watch_item: The comparative gains depend on the dataset and task correlation, so stacking may require careful validation to avoid overfitting and poor transfer to new welding conditions.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
